source: OCI policy reference (per-service 'Permissions Required for Each API Operation' tables)
notes: Maps an OCI SDK operation name (BaseClient.call_api operation_name) to the IAM permission(s) that a SUCCESSFUL call implies the caller holds.
Only permissions the docs explicitly list are recorded. Where an operation lists multiple permissions, ALL are required for success, so a 2xx response implies the caller holds ALL of them.

Some conditional permissions (e.g. KEY_DECRYPT only when a customer-managed key is used) are captured under 'conditional_permissions' and MUST NOT be recorded from a plain success -- they are informational only.
'operations' is a flat map keyed by operation name. This is safe for enumeration ops whose names are globally unique in the OCI SDK (ListInstances, ListBuckets, ListVaults, ...).

'ambiguous_operations' holds generic operation names that recur across services with DIFFERENT permissions (ListWorkRequests, GetWorkRequest, ListCertificates, ListShapes, ListPolicies, ListProtocols). These MUST be disambiguated by service before recording -- do NOT record them from the flat map.

ListShapes.note: core-services ListShapes; NOT the load-balancer ListShapes

ListPublicIps.note: reserved public IPs; ephemeral use PRIVATE_IP_READ

ListPolicies.note: identity ListPolicies; NOT the load-balancer ListPolicies

HeadObject.note: docs list OBJECT_READ or OBJECT_INSPECT; INSPECT is the weaker guaranteed floor

ListApplications.note: SDK operation_name is ListApplications (docs abbreviate as ListApp)

ListCertificates.note: load-balancer ListCertificates; API Gateway/others differ -- see ambiguous_operations

ambiguous_operations.__doc: Operation names that recur across services with DIFFERENT permissions. Disambiguate by service (the OCI SDK operation_name is identical; only the endpoint/service differs). Keys are service slugs.

verb_permission_sets.__doc: OCI verb -> permission-set expansion per resource-type, from the 'Details for Verb+ResourceType Combinations' tables. Access is cumulative: inspect < read < use < manage. Only resource-types with docs-confirmed sets are included.

instance-family._note: manage/use expand into many INSTANCE_* + VNIC_* + VOLUME_ATTACHMENT_* permissions; not fully enumerated here
